info.name: CareNest API
info.description:
Childcare & Transport Care Management Platform — B7A6 backend assignment.

Guardians book children into supervised care rooms run by verified staff, top up a wallet via real bKash Tokenized Checkout, book supervised transport, and rate staff. The core differentiator is a weighted waitlist priority engine that re-ranks and auto-promotes queued bookings on cancellation (see folders 7 and 8).

## How to run this
1. Start the API locally (`npm run dev`) or point `baseUrl` at a deployed instance.
2. Run `npx prisma db seed` at least once so the demo Admin account (`admin@carenest.com` / `CareNest@Admin2026`) exists.
3. Use the Collection Runner and run folders 1 through 14 top-to-bottom — folder 4 (Admin creates the Staff/Driver accounts) runs before folder 5 (Staff self-service logs into them). Folder 12 has two requests that need a real browser + bKash sandbox and are excluded from automated runs. Folder 14 is destructive (soft-deletes the demo Guardian and a Room) and deliberately sits at the very end — every other folder depends on records folder 14 removes.
4. Every response uses the standard envelope: `{ success, message, data }` on success, `{ success: false, message, errors: [] }` on error — HTTP status carries the code, never the body.

## Roles
GUARDIAN (self-registers), STAFF (SITTER | DRIVER | BOTH — created only by an Admin), ADMIN (seed-only, never via any API).

## Why cookies are disabled on this collection
The API sets httpOnly auth cookies on every login response, for real browsers. `POST /auth/refresh-token` deliberately checks that cookie *before* the request body (`getRefreshToken` in `auth.controller.ts` — "Cookie first (browsers), request body second (Postman / mobile clients)"). Postman's automatic cookie jar would otherwise silently clobber the `{{guardianAccessToken}}` flow the moment a second role logs in (its Set-Cookie overwrites the jar), so this collection disables cookie handling and relies purely on the Bearer token variables instead — exactly the "API client" path the backend was built to support.
